suggestions.rationale: Clinical Mapping Master Resolution 2026 publishes this relationship only as disease progression complication. Require documented periodontitis/periodontal disease and separately documented tooth loss attributable to periodontal attachment/bone loss. Do not infer cause of tooth loss when caries, trauma, extraction for other reasons, or other etiologies predominate. The cited literature supports only this bounded proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-11 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Longitudinal evidence found increased incident osteoporosis risk among people with periodontitis versus controls (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.12-1.75). Require periodontitis as the primary phenotype and separately diagnosed osteoporosis. Treat as longitudinal population-level risk/association only. Preserve age, sex/menopause, smoking, glucocorticoid exposure, nutritional status, endocrine disease, immobility, medications and other osteoporosis risks. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of periodontal-disease and osteoporosis
Documentation satisfying the approved phenotype restriction: clinically established periodontitis rather than nonspecific periodontal disease; osteoporosis separately diagnosed
Chronology and phenotype compatible with the bounded source proposition
Assessment of competing etiologies, shared risk factors, treatment/transplant context, and selection bias where applicable

Resolution of the approved publication guard: Require periodontitis as the primary phenotype and separately diagnosed osteoporosis. Treat as longitudinal population-level risk/association only. Preserve age, sex/menopause, smoking, glucocorticoid exposure, nutritional status, endocrine disease, immobility, medications and other osteoporosis risks.
